papers.title: On Quantised Magnetic Monopoles in the Nonlocal Electromagnetic Field
papers.abstract: We consider Maxwell electrodynamics in the presence of both electric and magnetic charges when the fields are made nonlocal by the prescription of the Moffat-Thompson nonlocal quantum field theory. The symmetry between the electric and magnetic equations is preserved, while a point magnetic charge is a finite distribution and its field energy becomes finite. When Dirac's quantisation condition $eg=2\pi n$ is imposed, the magnetic self-energy is found to be much greater than the corresponding electric one. We conclude that magnetic monopoles may be permitted by the theory and yet require a very large energy for their production, thus making their abundance and detection a difficult feat.

papers.title: A Clifford algebra approach to bosonic strings with fermionic boundaries
papers.abstract: The Brauer-Weyl (1935) theorem states that the algebra of tensor products of spinors is isomorphic to the Clifford (geometric) algebra, in any number of spacetime dimensions. The algebraic relation between fermions and bosons seen in the standard model agrees with the Brauer-Weyl theorem, but not with supersymmetry. It is commonly argued that string theory requires supersymmetry, on the grounds that nonsupersymmetric bosonic string theory (1) does not admit fermions, and (2) has an unstable tachyonic ground state. This paper rebuts those standard objections, pointing out that bosonic string theory admits ferm\-ions lying on a D-brane boundary of open strings, and that the open-string tachyon has all the properties of a Higgs field. The original 1970s formulation of bosonic string theory, re-envisaged as a theory of all the forces, not just the strong force, fits the standard model beautifully.

papers.title: Stronger-to-weaker gravity in generalized Brans-Dicke cosmology and implications for the Hubble and $S_8$ tensions
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of a Brans--Dicke-type scalar-tensor theory with non-minimal coupling $A(\phi)=1+c_1\phi+c_2\phi^2$ and power-law potentials $V(\phi)\propto\phi^{2n}$ ($n=2,3,4$), in which the dynamics of the scalar field yields a time-varying effective gravitational strength $G_{\rm eff}$. The theory is restricted to ghost-free solutions that also satisfy the dominant energy condition, sub-Planckian field ranges, as well as solar-system and big-bang nucleosynthesis bounds, keeping the scalar sector in a well-controlled and motivated regime. When confronting the model with Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernova data with the SH0ES calibration, the preferred scalar field dynamics lowers the sound horizon and raises the Hubble constant to $H_0=71.09\pm0.66\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for $n=3$, which also shows a moderate Bayesian preference over $\Lambda$CDM ($\ln B=4.55\pm0.44$) under the adopted priors. We show that, within this framework, the early stronger-gravity and late weaker-gravity phases compete for the same coefficients, forcing the latter to have amplitudes bounded by $1-G_{\rm eff}/G \lesssim 10^{-4}$. The data also prefer only brief weaker-gravity excursions after recombination for $n=2$ and $n=3$, lasting less than $0.1$ e-folds, but $n=4$ shows late-time transitions at $z\lesssim 3$ persisting for up to $\sim 1.9$ e-folds. In all cases the weaker-gravity regime is far too shallow to suppress the growth of structure: the $S_8$ parameter is in fact higher than in $\Lambda$CDM and the preferred cosmologies are of the early-modified-gravity type.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Type-3 New General Relativity on $\Lambda$CDM Background
papers.abstract: We investigate whether Type-3 New General Relativity can alleviate the cosmic growth tension. On a $\Lambda$CDM background, we derive the scalar perturbation equations and find the effective gravitational coupling to exceed Newton's constant throughout the parameter range compatible with ghost-free and background-hierarchy conditions. By confronting the theoretical model with growth-rate measurements from major galaxy redshift surveys, including WiggleZ, SDSS-IV eBOSS, BOSS, and VIPERS, we obtain constraints on the effective coupling that are consistent with the $\Lambda$CDM value. Consequently, the conditions for stability and tension reduction are mutually exclusive.

papers.title: Revisiting the Capacitance of a Hollow Metal Cylinder
papers.abstract: We complete the analysis of the capacitance of a hollow metal cylinder by deriving series representations for different aspect ratios and a practical formula that approximates the capacitance of the tube for any aspect ratio with an error below 1%.

papers.title: Gravitational lensing due to charged galactic wormhole
papers.abstract: We propose the back reaction to the charged galactic wormhole spacetime based on Yoshiaki Sofue's exponential dark matter density profile to find exact solutions. The charges act as an additional component to the static wormhole, which is primarily formed by the galactic dark matter density. Unlike traditional mass-based models, this solution incorporates charge effects within a realistic dark matter distribution, revealing unique interactions between dark matter, electromagnetic fields, and spacetime curvature. This study confirms the criteria for wormhole formation, designating it the "Charged Galactic Wormhole," and offers a new framework for investigating galactic structures, with potential observational signatures that deepen our understanding of dark matter and spacetime. Later, the proper radial distance and the embedding surface were also analyzed. Furthermore, the deflection of light around a charged galactic wormhole was investigated, along with a comprehensive review of the resulting image. The deflection of massive objects (charge less) near charged galactic wormholes is studied using the Gauss-Bonnet and Rindler-Ishak methods, with a detailed comparison of the results from both approaches. Additionally, in both the Rindler-Ishak (RI) and Gauss-Bonnet (GB) methods, when v tends to 1 i.e. when particle's velocity comparable to the speed of light , the results from these approaches converge, producing the same outcome as strong gravitational lensing.

papers.title: One-dimensional phase singularities as a source of atypical local oscillations
papers.abstract: In this work, phase singularities embedded in a wavepacket are shown to act as sources of atypical localized oscillations when the packet interacts with a linear system. We refer to these oscillations as chirpons, since they arise as strong variations of the instantaneous frequency (chirp). A mathematical expression is then provided to describe chirpons, and their behavior is explored through the interaction of a super-bandwidth wavepacket---containing two singularities---with a damped harmonic oscillator, a fundamental model for many physical systems. This interaction is analyzed theoretically, and the predictions are verified experimentally using a resonant electrical circuit as a realization of the oscillator. The results show that chirpons evolve in a manner fundamentally different from standard Fourier oscillations, revealing features of linear systems that are otherwise inaccessible. This introduces a new approach to analyze and characterize system responses, with potential applications in high-resolution spectroscopy and signal sensing.
